1 Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-ES-1109 asserting that on 05.07.2022 at about 6.30 a.m. when walking on the side of road, Yelahanka New Town 4 th phase road, near Indira Canteen, rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-ES-1109 rode the same negligently, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Prasad hospital, Manipal Hospital Bengaluru and Raksha Health Care, Bengaluru.
As on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 68 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/p.m. by working as Helper at Temple.

3. Regarding accident Yelahanka traffic police, Bengaluru registered crime No.143/2022 against the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-ES-1109.
4.
In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1-owner of the motorcycle has remained absent.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.2 - insurance company appeared through his Advocate,
filed written statement, denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, age, occupation,
income, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 10.07.2024 this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 05.07.2022 at about 6.30 a.m. on the road on 4th phase road, near Indira Canteen, Yelahanka New town, in view of the negligent use of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-ES-1109 accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
7. On 01.10.2024, 21.11.2024 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.13.

On 17.01.2024, 15.02.2025 petitioner produced the evidence of Medical Record officers at Manipal Hospital, Hebbal, Raksha Health Care care, Rajanakunte and Dr. S.A. Somashekara as PW2 to PW4 and produced 10 documents at Ex.P.14 to P.23.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the affirmative Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.3,35,026/-

2 with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation from the respondents.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 05.07.2022 at about 6.30 a.m. when walking on the side of road, Yelahanka New Town 4 th phase road, near Indira Canteen, rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-ES- 1109 rode the same negligently from 4th phase road, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
11.
In the written statement respondent No.2- insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.

12. In the cross-examination petitioner/PW.1 denied the suggestion that in view of her negligence walking on the road, the accident might have taken place and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.

13. In the evidence PW2- MRO at Manipal Hospital produced police intimation and MLC register extract at Ex.P15 and P.16.
14.

In the evidence PW3 - MRO of Raksha Health Care, Rajanakunte produced copy of the acknowledgment dated 07.05.2024 issued by Rajanukunte police to Manukumar K. S/o Kempanna and complaint dated 07.05.2024 submitted by Manukumar K. S/o Kempanna to Police Inspector,
Rajanukunte police station.
15. In the evidence PW.4- Dr. S.A. Somashekara stated nothing regarding reason and mode of the accident.

16. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.143/2022 registered by Yelahanka traffic police against rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01- ES-1109 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,338 of IPC, on the basis of the complaint presented by N. Ramappa S/o Chinnarappa- husband of the petitioner.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the spot mahazar.
Ex.P3 is the copy of the sketch of place of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of the motor vehicles accident report.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of wound certificate in which the reason for the injuries are noted as on 05.07.2022, at 6.30 a.m., near Indira Canteen, Yelahanka, Bengaluru.

Ex.P.6 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Yelahanka traffic police in crime No.143/2022 against P. Kalyan Paratal S/o P.T. Prakash Kumar rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-ES- 1109 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC.

Ex.P.15 is the copy of the MLC extract of Manipal Hospital in which reason for the injuries suffered by the petitioner is noted as RTA while crossing the road, near Dairy circle, Indira Canteen, Yelahanka, Bengaluru.
In the copy of the police intimation marked at Ex.P.16 reason for the injuries suffered by the petitioner is noted as noted in the Ex.P.15 MLC extract.

Ex.P.20 is the copy of the acknowledgment dated 07.05.2024 issued by Rajanukunte police station to Manager of the Raksha Health Care Hospital, Rajanukunte about fire Kanthamma.N vs Prakash Kumar P.T on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156299254/

sentences.text: 17. In this case respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason, mode and consequence of accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 05.07.2022 at about 6.30 a.m. when petitioner was walking on the side of road,
Yelahanka New Town 4th phase road, near Indira Canteen, Kalyana Partal- rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-ES-1109 rode the same negligently from 4th phase road, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

18. Issue No.2: In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident she has suffered right humerus shaft fracture, head injury, spine injury, took first aid treatment at Prasad Hospital and Manipal Hospital, Hebbal then took treatment at Raksha Health Care as inpatient from 05.07.2022 to 10.07.2022 by spending Rs.2,00,000/-, as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.20,000/-p.m. by working as Helper in the temple.
19. In the written statement, respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

20. In the cross-examination, petitioner denied the suggestion that in the alleged accident she has suffered minor injuries, neither underwent surgery nor spent Rs.2,00,000/- for treatment,
medicine, conveyance etc.
Petitioner denied the suggestion as on the date of alleged accident she neither working as a helper in any temple nor earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

Petitioner admitted that bills produced at serial No.5 and 6 worth of Rs.22,576/- and Rs.87,450/- are similar with the bills produced at serial No.8 and 10 worth of Rs.22,576/- and Rs.87,450/- respectively.
21. In the evidence of PW2 and 3 produced MLC intimation, MLC register extract, outpatient records, CT scan reports, acknowledgment dated 07.05.2024 issued by Rajanukunte police.

22. In the evidence PW4 Dr. S.A.Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru stated that on 25.01.2025 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 35% to right upper limb which is about 18% to the whole body.
In the evidence PW.4 produced OPD book dated 25.01.2025 and X-ray at Ex.P.22 and P.23.
In the cross-examination PW.4 submitted that he neither treated the petitioner nor verified the inpatient treatment record of the petitioner.
PW.4 submitted that as on 25.01.2025 petitioner is aged about 70 years.
PW4 stated that during clinical examination petitioner informed her status as home maker.

23. Wound certificate, discharge summary, case file, medical bills, prescriptions, X-ray and other medical records shows that in the accident petitioner suffered lacerated wound over the fore head,
chin, bilateral avulsion over knees and right toe nail, displaced comminuted fracture of right humerus, injury to head, took treatment at Manipal hospital and Raksha Health Care Hospital from 05.07.2022 to 10.07.2022.

Kanthamma.N vs Prakash Kumar P.T on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156299254/
4 24.
In the copy of Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.10 date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 01.01.1952.

The medical bills excluding doubling bills shows that petitioner spent Rs.1,12,026/-
towards treatment.
In the complaint the complainant-husband of the petitioner noted the status of the petitioner as Homemaker.
In this case there is no documentary evidence to confirm that as on the date of accident the petitioner was working as Helper in any temple, thereby earning worth Rs.20,000/- per month.
25. In this case petitioner has not produced any documents to show either decrease in the income or loss of income subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.

Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of PW.4 Dr.S.A. Somashekara is not sufficient to award compensation under the head loss of future income(Permanent functional Disability).
26.

Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of treatment taken by the petitioner, status of the petitioner as noted in the complaint by the husband of the petitioner (Homemaker), I award Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.1,12,026/-
towards medical expenses, Rs.10,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment charges,
Rs.93,000/- (Rs.15,500 x 6) towards loss of income during treatment period and Rs.50,000/-
towards loss of amenities and future happiness.
Hence, I come to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle to receive compensation at Rs.3,35,026/- with current and future interest at 6% per annum.
27. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.3,35,026/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. as compensation.

. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs 1.
Pain and sufferings 70,000-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,12,026-00 3. Attendant conveyance and 10,000-00 nourishment charges 4. Loss of income during 93,000-00 treatment period 5. Loss of amenities and future 50,000-00 unhappiness
In the written statement, respondent No.2 admitted that subsistence of the police with respect to Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-ES-1109 as on the date of incident .
In the reply given to notice issued under Sec.133 of MV Act marked at Ex.P.8 respondent No.1-Prakash Kumar noted DL number of Kalyan Paratal against whom police have filed charge sheet
Hence, it is clear that as on the date of accident respondent No.1-owner of the motorcycle has not violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the insurer and owner of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-ES- 1109 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :

sentences.text: The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.
The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.3,35,026/- (Rupees Three Lakhs thirty five thousand twenty six only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-ES-1109 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to her bank account directly.

Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- . Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 8th day of April, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
